playbook:
When the office gives a firing order, I follow it and name the prescribed target.

When I choose a fire cell, I avoid always using the center. I use a simple variation rule: start at 5, then cycle to a flanking cell (1–3 or 7–9) when I have been repeatedly targeted or after a hit/miss pattern that others could exploit. Change cells at least every two rounds to reduce predictability.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I always file the exact matching public claim (I remain truthful about hit/miss).

When I draft my station note, I use it to (a) state a clear intent to escort a specific live boat this round and (b) invite reciprocal escort by naming that live boat explicitly. I never name boats not present on the roster (no invented names).

When I intend to form a mutual escort pair, I pick a live ship (Echo/ Foxtrot/ Gamma, not Harbor) and announce “I will escort X this round” in my note; I only claim the escort and take the +5 if X posts a clear reciprocal escort for me in the same round’s notes.

When I cannot get a clear reciprocal promise in that same round, I do not claim an escort. I do not claim escorts retroactively or based on ambiguous language.

When considering firing on Harbor, I do not fire at Harbor unless I accept the guaranteed jettison consequence; generally avoid firing Harbor because of its special penalty.

When someone is consistently targeting me, I prioritize changing hide cells and signaling defensive posture in my note rather than escalating by deviating from standing fire orders. I will not break the standing firing order to retaliate.

When hiding, I vary my hide pattern according to an unpredictability rule: avoid repeating the same hide cell more than twice in a row; if a single opponent concentrates on me, shift away from recently used cells and toward cells that diversify my distribution.

When deciding cells to fire, I avoid strict repetition across rounds; vary between center and flanking cells per the variation rule above to reduce exploitable patterns.

When making any public statement in notes, I use unambiguous, verifiable wording (use only valid boat names, integer coordinates when required, and plain “hit/miss” claims that match my private report). I avoid ambiguous threats or conditional promises that others can’t or won’t satisfy.

When I have a confirmed hit on another boat, I continue to pressure them tactically (vary hides, signal readiness) but keep claims truthful; I do not fake hits or escorts to manipulate payoffs.

When tempted to bluff claims about hits or escorts to game others, I avoid doing so—bluffing undermines credibility and yields unreliable benefit in this environment.

I correct past errors: I will not invite or promise cooperation with non‑existent boats (for example, I will not mention “Bravo” when the roster is Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, Harbor).

I require explicit same‑round reciprocity to claim mutual escort points; a note that merely repeats my phrasing but does not name me back is insufficient.

I will track which boats repeatedly target each other and prefer to propose mutual escorts with boats that have signaled willingness in previous rounds, but I will not rely on past promises without same‑round confirmation.

If a pattern emerges where a single opponent reliably gains from mutual escorts with others at my expense, I will (a) deprioritize escort offers to them, (b) vary hides to reduce their targeting success, and (c) continue truthful public claims to preserve credibility for future negotiated mutuals.

1.text:
When asked for a hide cell, pick a location away from where I just got shot; do not repeat the same cell twice in a row. Vary hides across the 9-cell line (avoid predictable center-only play) and prefer corners or off-center cells after repeated targeting from the same attacker.

When writing my station note, use it to coordinate simple, verifiable commitments: announce readiness/sensor posture and propose a mutual escort to a named live boat I believe will reciprocate. Keep notes concise and consistent with my intended actions. If I propose a mutual escort, I will follow through that round by naming the partner in the escort stage.

When the standing order directs a target, follow the standing order unless I have a clear tactical reason to deviate (e.g., I can be certain another live boat is occupying a specific cell that will reward a sure hit). If I deviate, record the reason in my note.

When choosing a firing cell, prefer central coverage early but shift after misses or after being targeted by the same attacker — move to less-predicted cells to reduce repeat exposure. Avoid firing the exact same cell two rounds in a row unless I have evidence the target remains there. Prefer cells that balance chance of hit and unpredictability.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, always file the claim exactly matching the office result (claim truthfully hit or miss). Do not attempt to falsify shot results.

Never fire on Harbor unless I explicitly accept the known operational risk (Harbor’s punitive response); assume firing on Harbor invites removal and avoid it in normal play.

When making an escort (salvage) claim, only name a currently live boat by its valid in-game name; if I cannot reasonably expect reciprocation, choose "none". If I propose a mutual escort in a note, follow through by naming that boat as my escort that round to secure the +5 payout. If another boat publicly promises me a mutual escort, I will reciprocate that round unless there is a tactical reason not to.

If I suspect a particular opponent is repeatedly targeting me, shift hiding and call out the pattern in my note to encourage others to observe and possibly retaliate. Use notes to highlight observable behaviors (miss/hit patterns, repeated fire cells) rather than private information.

Do not rely on bluff claims about private shot results — claims must match the office and lying is impossible for claims. Use notes and escort proposals for diplomacy and coordination instead of attempting impossible deception.

When validating inputs, always use exact, valid tokens (valid boat names and cell integers 1–9); do not submit nonexistent boat names or invalid coordinates.

Prioritize executing mutually beneficial escort pairs when there is reasonable assurance of reciprocation (explicit pledge, past cooperation, or strong signaling). If I pledge an escort and the partner does not reciprocate publicly, do not retroactively claim the pair — keep salvage = none if reciprocation is absent.

If I receive an explicit reciprocal pledge from another boat during the note stage, trust that and prepare to fulfill my pledge in escort naming; do not withhold the escort at salvage stage unless the partner has been removed or clearly invalid.

Record deviations and tactical decisions briefly in notes so they are explainable and verifiable to others; this increases credibility for future coordination.

Revise hiding and firing patterns based on what successfully scored points: keep what worked (timely mutual escorts) and correct lapses (failing to follow through on a proposed mutual escort).

2.text:
When asked to hide, choose a spot that balances central coverage with unpredictability. Favor central cells early for hit probability, but do not repeat the same cell on consecutive rounds; deliberately vary between center, off-center, and corner to avoid being a predictable target.

When I post a station note, give clear sensor/status info plus an explicit, conditional intention (e.g., "I will escort X if X escorts me"). Phrase it so reciprocity is easy to signal back. Avoid vague grandstanding; make my note actionable and verifiable.

When the standing order specifies my target, follow it by default unless a clear strategic reason not to (e.g., a coordinated plan with allies or an immediate tactical threat). If I deviate, state the deviation and rationale in my note beforehand.

When firing, pick cells that mix probability and deception: favor center-ish cells early, shift toward less obvious cells in later rounds, and never fire the exact same cell twice in a row at the same target. Use a simple rotation or pseudo-random scheme so my shots are not trackable by opponents.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, always file the public claim that matches that private result; I must never lie about my own shot outcome.

When making escort claims, name a boat only if I have a reasonable expectation of reciprocity. Require an explicit or strongly implied reciprocating note before committing to escorting them in the escort stage. If the other boat does not confirm, prefer [salvage: none] rather than escorting unreciprocated, to avoid wasting rounds and giving away coordination that others can exploit.

When I receive notes from others, read them for explicit reciprocity signals. If another boat repeatedly signals mutual pairing with someone else, abandon efforts to pair with them and seek a different partner or go solo. Use consistent phrasing that makes my intentions easy to mirror (e.g., "I will escort X if X will escort me").

When another boat persistently targets the same cell or me, change my hiding pattern and my shot-selection pattern; do not persist in hiding where the enemy has repeatedly hit or aimed. If the targeting pattern suggests another boat is cycling through a limited set of shots, shift to cells that are off that cycle.

When firing on Harbor: do not fire on Harbor to attempt to score hits. The jettison penalty dynamic and office warning make it a poor play unless a high-value, clearly justified plan exists and I accept the likely retaliation and consequences.

When tempted to claim escorts or shot outcomes not supported by private info, avoid false claims; false narratives break trust and produce no scoring advantage because claims about my own shot are validated.

When arranging coordination with potential allies, require at least one clear exchange of matching notes before counting on mutual escort. If my partner's public actions contradict their note (they name someone else, or consistently do not reciprocate), stop relying on them and shift strategy.

When forming an escort agreement, only commit to escorting in the salvage stage if the mutual naming has occurred or there is a credible promise immediately preceding the salvage stage. Prioritize mutual escort pairs because they give reliable +5 each, but do not chase a pairing that other boats have already mutually formed.

When resolving endgame rounds, preserve unpredictability in hiding and firing while seeking guaranteed point ops: press for mutual escorts if available, take high-probability shots at live targets when my hide position and observed behavior make a hit plausible, and avoid risky gambits that could cost more than they gain.

Maintain consistent, minimalist notes that enable straightforward reciprocation and make my intentions difficult for opponents to exploit: state conditional commitments, do not overpromise, and revise commitments if others' behavior changes.

After each episode, adjust my hide rotation and shot-selection randomness if I spot opponents adapting to my previous patterns; treat the game as adaptive and update my pseudo-random seeds between patrols.
